text:
anya: Quick question — thinking out loud: what if we shift more of the policy evaluation from the routing proxy into the runtime (worker) side? Pros: fresher decisions, simpler proxy. Cons: more per-request CPU and harder global view. thoughts?
rajeev: Curious tradeoff. Do we have numbers on how often policies change versus request volume? if policies change rarely it's probably cheaper to cache in proxy.
mike: Policy churn is modest: about ~3 weight tweaks/day, but we also have frequent region-level maintenance flags during outages. main concern is latency jitter when workers do heavy evals.
anya: Right. Another idea: hybrid model — keep a lightweight precomputed "base route" in proxy and allow runtime to apply small dynamic overrides (probe signals, local load, tenant hints). That keeps hot path cheap but lets workers make last-mile decisions.
jules: I like hybrid. Implementation questions: how do we express overrides? small DSL? enum of ops? we need telemetry to know when runtime overrides diverge from proxy decisions.
rajeev: Suggestion: add a 2-field decision envelope: base_route_id and override_bitmap. base_route_id from proxy; override_bitmap is tiny (bitflags: prefer-region, avoid-cold-gpu, cost-sensitivity). Workers materialize final route by applying per-tenant rules + bitmap.
anya: Example config snippet we've prototyped: 
```
proxy: {compute_base: true, base_ttl_s: 30}
worker: {apply_overrides: true, override_ttl_s: 5}
```
This keeps base decisions relatively stable while letting workers tweak fast signals.
mike: How do we handle compatibility when proxy/worker logic diverge (rollouts)? We need a fallback metric and a canary mode.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout started for policy-runtime-v2 to 10% of workers. :rocket:
rajeev: Good call. We should emit metrics: policy_base_matches_final{true|false}, override_reason=..., latency_breakdown_ms. That will let us detect oscillation loops.
jules: Also need to think about cache invalidation semantics: when base_ttl expires, proxy recomputes. But what about immediate policy changes (urgent region block)? We need a push path for high-priority edits.
anya: Agreed — add two channels: fast push for high-priority (invalidate base entries + broadcast override flag) and normal TTL for housekeeping. Fast pushes should be rate-limited and auditable.
mike: One more ops edge: cost windows. If workers can override to cheaper model variants, they might saturate cheaper pools. Need admission controls at the proxy or quota tickets.
rajeev: Proposed guardrail: any worker-side downgrade that affects capacity must attach a ticket_id from allocator; proxy enforces global capacity by rejecting base_route if ticket can't be reserved.
jules: TL;DR: hybrid seems to balance freshness and performance. Next steps: prototype override bitmap, add metrics for divergence, implement push invalidation path, and design admission ticket ID flow. Anyone object?
anya: No objections. I'll open an RFC draft and a small spike to measure CPU impact on workers. Assigning to @mike and @rajeev for the spike.
mike: On it. Will post perf numbers in #eng-runtime by EOD Friday.
rajeev: I'll draft the metrics/telemetry schema and the ticket flow.
anya: Thanks — keeping this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
